question: Why does ViT split an image into patches before applying a transformer?
direct_answer: Because transformers expect a sequence of tokens, so patches provide a tokenized representation of the image.
expanded_answer: A transformer does not directly consume a 2D image grid in the same way a convolutional network does. Patch splitting turns local regions of the image into discrete units that can be flattened, embedded, and passed as a sequence, making the image compatible with self-attention.
key_points: Flattened patches are projected into embeddings
This bridges images and sequence models
common_wrong_ideas: Patch splitting is only for reducing image resolution
The patch size does not matter
The transformer can only work on text tokens
